title: The certificate authority and trusted machines (ship-fleet ca show --json, version 1)
description: Printed by `ship-fleet ca show --json` on the FleetLedger computer: the CA keys' fingerprints, each Ship's host certificate from its last status poll, and the machines trusted to attach. Read from ships.toml and the status cache only: it asks no Ship and issues nothing. See contracts/ship-fleet.md.

host_ca.description: The key that signs Ships' host certificates.

user_ca.description: The user CA keys Ships accept, the current one first (then any kept during a rotation).

ships.description: Every Ship in the inventory, in its order.

certificate_valid_before.description: When its host certificate ends; null: none, or it never ends.

principals.description: The names its host certificate is valid for.

needs.description: Why ship-fleet ca sign would sign it again; tooling update: its tooling predates certificates, or it was never seen. null: nothing to do.

trust_behind.description: Its user CA keys or revocation list are not the current ones.

seen.description: A status of it was ever fetched; false: the rest says nothing about it yet.

machines.description: Every machine ever trusted (ship-fleet trust), untrusted ones included, by name.

scope.description: Which Ships its certificates open: all, tag:<tag>, ship:<name>.

logins.description: What its certificates log in as on those Ships (ship-fleet trust NAME --logins): agent (attaches to the agent) and/or owner (the fleet owner's own login, with sudo), in that order. Added in this version; a FleetLedger from before prints none.

valid_before.description: When its last certificate ends (UTC, RFC 3339, Z); null: none issued yet.

revoked.description: When ship-fleet untrust revoked it; it stays so.

fingerprint.description: Its own public key's, as ssh-keygen -l prints it. No two entries that are not revoked share a key, so a machine finds its own live entry, and its trusted name, as the one with its key's fingerprint and revoked null; revoked entries with the same fingerprint may be listed too.

state.description: Its last certificate: ok; expiring (its last day, or the last half of a shorter lifetime); lapsed; none (never issued); revoked.

this_computer.description: It is the FleetLedger computer itself (ship-fleet trust --this-computer), which renews its own certificate.

last_refreshed.description: When it last got its own bundle (ship-fleet machine-bundle); null: it never asked, so it does not refresh itself.

idle_limit.description: true (the default): after 30 days without asking it is refused its bundle until allowed again (ship-fleet trust NAME --allow-again); false: it stays trusted until untrusted.

idle_refused.description: When ship-fleet machine-bundle first refused it for being idle; null unless it is refused now.

timestamp.description: UTC, RFC 3339, with a Z suffix.
